statements.impact_statement: CVE-2020-8911 (GHSA-f5pg-7wfw-84q9, GO-2022-0646): the V1 encryption client of the AWS S3 Crypto SDK for Go (github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/service/s3/s3crypto) is open to a CBC padding-oracle attack on objects encrypted with AES-CBC. AWS added V2 clients in aws-sdk-go 1.34.0, while the Go vulnerability database lists the V1 s3crypto clients as affected in every version (https://github.com/google/security-research/security/advisories/GHSA-f5pg-7wfw-84q9, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2022-0646, https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/pull/3403). Read every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, 1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16, on amd64 and arm64 (1.21.2-0 was published for arm64 only); 87 packages, with no debug-symbol packages published for this source. Every build lists github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go 1.55.8 in the Go build information of /usr/bin/alloy, but in no build does the program contain any function from the s3crypto package, checked against the function names the Go linker records in each binary. As a control, the same search finds functions from github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace in every build. The vulnerable S3 encryption client is not compiled in. As a positive control for the s3crypto search, the same go tool nm search on a test program built against aws-sdk-go 1.55.8 that calls s3crypto.NewEncryptionClient and s3crypto.NewDecryptionClient lists both functions and 21 s3crypto functions in all.
